title.narrative: ADB Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility
ADB Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility

description.narrative: CEFs huvudsakliga mål är att finansiera projekt inom "ren Energi", dvs. förnybart, energieff, och tillgång till energi. Fonden finansierar även pilotprojekt, utveckling av policy, finansieringsmetoder etc. för att stimulere ren energi.

Clean Energy Fund is part of ADB Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility. Main objective to finance projects in clean energy, major demonstration projects, policy development and mode of fundings.

The Clean Energy Financing Partnership Facility (CEFPF) was established in 2007 to help improve energy security in Developing Member Countries (DMCs) and decrease the rate of climate change. It will do this by financing the deployment of new, more efficient and less polluting supply and end-use technologies, through either grant or non-grant resources. The CEFPF is composed of the Clean Energy Fund (CEF), the Asian Clean Energy Fund (ACEF), the Carbon Capture and Storage Fund (CCSF) and the Canadian Climate Fund for the Private Sector in Asia (CFPS).

sector.narrative: Energy generation, renewable sources - multiple technologies

description.narrative:
Key Achievements (2025):
- Mobilized significant clean energy investments by leveraging US$11.1 billion in total investments, achieving a 1:33 leverage ratio, where every US$1 of CEFPF financing mobilized US$33 of clean energy investment from ADB and development partners.
- Allocated US$10.7 million to 12 new projects in 2025, bringing cumulative allocations to US$349.7 million across 279 projects since the facility was established.
- Contributed to major climate mitigation outcomes, with supported projects expected to reduce 33.8 million tCOe annually, install 3,107 MW of renewable energy capacity, and generate 11.2 TWh of renewable electricity each year.
- Expanded deployment of innovative clean energy technologies to 56 technologies across 37 developing member countries, including first-of-its-kind floating solar, battery energy storage, smart grids, geothermal, and digital energy solutions.
- Maintained strong commitment to gender equality, with 81% of supported projects promoting gender equality, exceeding ADB's corporate target for 2030.
Examples of how results have contributed to desirable changes among important actors:
The CEFPF has contributed to several tangible changes among key actors in the energy sector by strengthening institutional capacity, improving policy and regulatory frameworks, and enhancing the readiness of governments and markets to invest in clean energy. The following are examples:
- For governments and public institutions, CEFPF-supported technical assistance has strengthened the enabling environment for clean energy investments. In Uzbekistan, the completed technical assistance on distributed solar photovoltaic (PV) systems supported the development of regulatory frameworks, technical guidelines, and implementation roadmaps, while training more than 50 government officials and energy specialists. These outputs have informed subsequent ADB investment planning and contributed to increased institutional readiness for scaling distributed solar energy.
- The facility has also strengthened the capacity of energy institutions across the region. By the end of 2025, CEFPF had supported 672 training events, workshops, and conferences, reaching more than 28,000 participants, including nearly 6,000 women. These activities have enhanced the technical and institutional capacities of government agencies, utilities, and other stakeholders to design, implement, and manage clean energy initiatives.
- For private sector actors, the CEFPF has helped reduce investment barriers and improve project bankability. In the Philippines, the Geothermal Resource Derisking Facility is expected to lower exploration risks through independent technical reviews, encouraging private developers to invest in geothermal projects that were previously considered too risky. This is expected to unlock new geothermal investments and accelerate the country's renewable energy transition.
